heading: West Virginia Paycheck Calculator

parts.markdown:
Use our free West Virginia paycheck calculator to estimate your take-home pay after federal income tax, West Virginia income tax, Social Security, Medicare and applicable municipal service fees.

Enter your annual salary or hourly wage, select your payment frequency and customize your withholding information to understand how much money you could receive on payday.

West Virginia reduced its individual income tax rates again in 2026. Employees working in certain cities may also have local service fees deducted from their earnings.

Whether you work in Charleston, Huntington, Morgantown, Parkersburg or another West Virginia community, understanding your payroll deductions can help you compare employment opportunities and manage household expenses.

## How to Use the West Virginia Paycheck Calculator

Choose annual salary or hourly wages and select the pay schedule shown on your pay stub. Hourly employees can enter their regular hours and qualifying overtime.

Enter the federal and West Virginia income tax withheld for that pay period. Use the full withholding amounts, including any additional withholding.

Enter any municipal service fee withheld from that pay period in the local withholding field.

Include employee retirement contributions, eligible health premiums and other deductions from the same pay period. Enter each deduction once.

Enter prior year-to-date taxable wages if you are approaching a Social Security or Additional Medicare threshold.


## West Virginia Payroll Taxes in 2026

Visit the [West Virginia Tax Division](https://tax.wv.gov/) for official individual income tax and employer withholding information.

## West Virginia Income Tax Changes in 2026

West Virginia enacted additional income tax reductions through Senate Bill 392 in March 2026.

The revised annual income tax rates apply retroactively to January 1, 2026.

For taxpayers other than married individuals filing separately, the annual tax brackets are:

Read the official West Virginia 2026 income tax rate reduction guidance for details.

## Understanding West Virginia Form IT-104

Employees generally complete Form IT-104 to communicate their withholding exemptions and applicable withholding selections to their employers.

The state recognizes an annual withholding exemption value of $2,000 per qualifying exemption.

These amounts reduce wages used in the withholding calculation.

West Virginia also distinguishes between the standard two-earner or multiple-job withholding schedule and an optional one-earner schedule.

Employees should not automatically select the lower withholding schedule solely to increase their take-home pay.

Obtain the appropriate certificate through the West Virginia withholding forms directory.

## How to Calculate West Virginia Income Tax Withholding

Consider an employee receiving $2,500 in biweekly taxable wages and claiming one applicable withholding exemption.

Assume the revised March 2026 two-earner withholding schedule applies.

Adjusted taxable wages:

$2,500 − $76.92 = $2,423.08.

The applicable highest biweekly withholding bracket begins at $1,731.

The published base tax is $56.27, and the marginal rate is 4.58%.

Estimated withholding:

$56.27 + (($2,423.08 − $1,731) × 4.58%).

The unrounded result is approximately $87.97.

Using nearest-dollar withholding, the estimated deduction is $88.

Review the official West Virginia percentage method of withholding, IT-100.2.A for applicable payroll-period schedules.

## West Virginia Municipal Service Fees

Certain West Virginia municipalities impose fixed fees on individuals working within city boundaries.

These fees differ from ordinary percentage-based personal income taxes.

For example, Huntington imposes a $5 weekly City Service Fee on applicable individuals working within the city.

An employee working two covered weeks would ordinarily have a $10 deduction.

Other municipalities may have different rates, exemptions, collection requirements and rules for employees working multiple jobs.

Visit the official Huntington City Service Fee guidance and Charleston municipal government website for applicable requirements.

Do not assume that every West Virginia employee pays a municipal service fee.

## Federal Taxes Deducted From West Virginia Paychecks

Federal income tax withholding depends on taxable earnings, filing status, payroll frequency and Form W-4 information.

Employers follow the calculation methods in [IRS Publication 15-T](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15t).

Employees generally contribute 6.2% of covered wages toward Social Security, up to $184,500 in 2026.

Ordinary Medicare withholding applies at 1.45% of covered earnings.

Additional Medicare withholding of 0.9% generally applies when covered wages paid by an employer exceed $200,000 during the calendar year.

Read the [IRS Employer's Tax Guide](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15) and Social Security Administration contribution limits for official information.

## West Virginia Paycheck Example: $65,000 Salary

Consider an employee earning $65,000 annually and receiving $2,500 biweekly.

Assume ordinary single federal withholding settings, one West Virginia withholding exemption and the revised two-earner state withholding schedule.

If the employee also owes a $10 municipal service fee for two covered working weeks in Huntington, estimated take-home pay would decrease to $1,994.60.

This example assumes no employee benefit deductions or reached annual federal payroll contribution limits.

## West Virginia Hourly Paycheck Calculator

Suppose an employee earns $25 per hour and works 40 regular hours plus eight qualifying overtime hours at time-and-a-half.

Regular earnings: $1,000.

Overtime earnings: $300.

Total gross earnings: $1,300.

Applicable federal and West Virginia taxes are then calculated using their respective taxable wage amounts.

Local service fees may apply independently of the employee's hourly earnings.

Review the West Virginia Division of Labor and [US Department of Labor overtime guidance](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/overtime) for applicable employment requirements.

## Working Across West Virginia State Borders

West Virginia has reciprocal income tax arrangements with certain neighboring states.

Eligible employees may qualify for different state withholding treatment based on residence, employment location and applicable documentation.

However, state income tax reciprocity does not necessarily eliminate municipal service fees.

Consult the West Virginia Tax Division and applicable municipal authorities before claiming an exemption.

## Managing Your West Virginia Take-Home Income

Use estimated net earnings rather than gross salary when establishing spending limits.

Account for housing, transportation, groceries, healthcare, utilities and required debt payments.

Employees receiving substantial overtime or seasonal compensation should estimate income across several representative pay periods.

Our [emergency fund calculator](/savings/emergency-fund-calculator/) can help establish a savings target, while our [salary-to-hourly calculator](/calculators/salary-to-hourly-calculator/) can help compare different compensation arrangements.

The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau also offers financial education resources.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### What is West Virginia's income tax rate in 2026?

The revised individual income tax rates range from 2.11% to 4.58%. Actual paycheck withholding depends on the applicable employer schedule and employee exemptions.

### Does Huntington deduct a city service fee from paychecks?

Yes. Huntington imposes a $5 weekly service fee on applicable individuals working within city boundaries.

### Why are there two West Virginia withholding schedules?

The two-earner schedule generally helps prevent insufficient withholding for employees with multiple jobs or working spouses. An optional one-earner schedule may apply according to the employee's withholding certificate.
